name: Reginhardus Sigebergensis
untranslatedHighlights: Reginhard, 2nd abbot of Michaelsberg/Siegburg (d. 1105); commissioned the Vita Annonis; his own PL work has no English translation located in any search

name: Honorius II
modernTranslations: Papal writings not clearly translated; Grimoire of Pope Honorius III (different work, later, 17th-18th c.)
untranslatedHighlights: Papal correspondence and writings remain largely untranslated

name: Fredegarius Scholasticus Burgundiae
modernTranslations: Wallace-Hadrill translation 1960; Historia Epitomata translated (third book)
untranslatedHighlights: Chronicle of Fredegar available in translation; parts translated by Wallace-Hadrill

name: Anastasius IV
modernTranslations: Some letters preserved; treatise on Trinity documented but translation status unclear
untranslatedHighlights: Papal works largely in Latin; limited English translation material found

name: Basilius Caesareae
pdTranslations: NPNF2-08: Basil: Letters and Select Works
modernTranslations: NPNF translation by Blomfield Jackson; Rule of St Basil Latin-English edition
untranslatedHighlights: Major works well covered in NPNF2-08; comprehensive English translation available

name: Zacchaeus Christianus
modernTranslations: Work is the anonymous Consultationes Zacchaei et Apollonii (c.408-410); modern French translation in Sources Chretiennes 401-402 (Feiertag & Steinmann 1994); no English translation located
untranslatedHighlights: Consultationes Zacchaei et Apollonii - three-book Christian-pagan dialogue apology, untranslated into English despite modern French SC edition

name: Auctor incertus (Isidorus Hispalensis?)
modernTranslations: Anonymous/uncertain attribution; Isidore of Seville's genuine works have modern translations if correctly attributed
untranslatedHighlights: Uncertain authorship precludes definitive translation status

name: Joannes S. Arnulfi Metensis
modernTranslations: Known for Historia Translationis Sanctae Glodesindis (c.977-983); no modern English translation located
untranslatedHighlights: Hagiographic works documented but translation status unclear

name: Candidus Fuldensis
modernTranslations: Vita S. Eigil (prose & verse, c.840) and philosophical aphorisms; no English translation located
untranslatedHighlights: Carolingian scholar; works remain in Latin; philosophical texts documented but not translated

name: Eusebius Caesariensis
pdTranslations: NPNF translations; Life of Constantine (McGiffert); Ecclesiastical History (multiple)
modernTranslations: Loeb Classical Library edition; Jeremy Schott recent translation (UC Press); multiple modern translations
untranslatedHighlights: Ecclesiastical History is the most translated major early Christian historical work

name: Eusebius Pamphilus
pdTranslations: NPNF2-01: Church History, Life of Constantine, Oration in Praise of Constantine
modernTranslations: Samuel Parker translation 1703; NPNF translation; Loeb Classical Library; modern translations available
untranslatedHighlights: Major church father with extensive English translation coverage

name: Rudolfus I
modernTranslations: No significant writings documented; likely administrative figure (Holy Roman Emperor-elect)
untranslatedHighlights: Historical figure; no substantial body of personal writings known to be translated

name: Raimundus de Agiles
modernTranslations: Hill & Hill translation 1968 (American Philosophical Society); Currie 2024 translation (Routledge, Crusade Texts in Translation); Fordham sourcebook excerpts
untranslatedHighlights: Historia Francorum qui ceperunt Iherusalem well covered in English translations

name: Julianus Pomerius
modernTranslations: Suelzer translation in Ancient Christian Writers vol. 4 (1947); available through Logos, Faithlife
untranslatedHighlights: De Vita Contemplativa fully translated in ACW series

name: Bertholdus Constantiensis
modernTranslations: Annales/chronicles documented; no English translation located
untranslatedHighlights: Berthold of Constance; medieval chronicles preserved but translation status unclear

name: Osbernus Cantuariensis
modernTranslations: Hagiographic works including Vita Sancti Dunstani; modern scholarly translations of saints' lives
untranslatedHighlights: Known for musical treatises and hagiography; partial translation coverage

name: Auctor incertus (Prosper Aquitanus?)
modernTranslations: If these works include pseudo-Prosper's De vocatione omnium gentium, that was translated by P. De Letter (ACW 14, 1952, 'The Call of All Nations')
untranslatedHighlights: Uncertain authorship; the major pseudo-Prosper treatise has an ACW English translation

name: Adamnanus Hiiensis
modernTranslations: Vita Columbae (Life of Columba) translated by Richard Sharpe and James Rose Macpherson; De Locis Sanctis translated
untranslatedHighlights: Major works including Vita Columbae well-covered in modern English translation

name: Odilo V Cluniacensis
modernTranslations: Vita S. Maioli and Epitaphium writings documented; letters and sermons preserved but translation status varies
untranslatedHighlights: Benedictine abbot's works documented but comprehensive English translation unclear

name: Ferrandus diaconus
modernTranslations: Breviatio Canonum (canon law epitome, 232 canons) documented; English translation status unclear
untranslatedHighlights: Canonical works preserved in Latin; translation to English not clearly documented

name: Willelmus Conquestor
modernTranslations: Official writs and charters preserved; no substantial personal writings known to be translated
untranslatedHighlights: Historical figure; administrative documents preserved but minimal literary output

name: Lambertus Atrebatensis
modernTranslations: Letters survive including correspondence with Countess Clemence of Flanders (translated at Epistolae project); comprehensive translation status unclear
untranslatedHighlights: Ecclesiastical correspondence documented; English translation not clearly available

name: Wilhelmus Daniae
modernTranslations: William of Aebelholt (d. Easter 1203, Denmark); two books of letters in PL 209; the Life OF William translated in Victorine Texts in Translation, but his own letters have no located English translation (scholarly edition in Diplomatarium Danicum)
untranslatedHighlights: Extensive letter collection - key source for 12th-c. Danish church history - untranslated into English

name: Benedictinus anonymus
modernTranslations: Anonymous Benedictine author; PL contains many such anonymous liturgical/monastic compilations
untranslatedHighlights: Anonymous work; translation status cannot be determined

name: Eustathius
modernTranslations: Commentary on Odyssey translated by Cullhed & Olson (Brill); Capture of Thessaloniki translated by Melville-Jones; Commentary on Iliad not translated to English
untranslatedHighlights: Byzantine scholar (c.1115-1196); Odyssey commentary translated, Iliad commentary remains untranslated

name: Auctor incertus (Walafridus Strabo?)
modernTranslations: Uncertain author; Walafrid Strabo's genuine works have partial coverage (e.g., Visio Wettini trans. Traill; Hortulus) if correctly attributed
untranslatedHighlights: Uncertain authorship; much pseudo-Walafrid material (e.g., Glossa Ordinaria attributions) untranslated

name: Innocentius I
modernTranslations: 36 letters preserved in NPNF and other sources; letters to Jerome, Bishop Exuperius documented
untranslatedHighlights: Papal correspondence available in English through NPNF and early church text repositories

name: Ogerius Lucedii
modernTranslations: Oglerio di Lucedio (c.1136-1214), Cistercian abbot; Tractatus in laudibus Sancte Dei Genitricis (13 sermons), Planctus Beatae Virginis Mariae; no English translation located in any search
untranslatedHighlights: Marian sermons and Planctus of a notable Cistercian abbot remain untranslated

name: Felix III
modernTranslations: Complete English translation of correspondence available at The See of Peter website; not in NPNF (post-Leonine)
untranslatedHighlights: Pope Felix III (483-492) correspondence fully translated at theseeofpeter.com

name: Guitmundus Aversanus
modernTranslations: De corporis et sanguinis Christi veritate translated (Vaillancourt); Corpus Christianorum in Translation series 'On the Body and Blood of the Lord'
untranslatedHighlights: Medieval Benedictine theologian; Eucharistic works translated, minor works may remain in Latin

name: Auctor incertus (Hincmarus Rhemensis?)
modernTranslations: Uncertain author; genuine Hincmar works have growing English coverage (De divortio, Manchester UP 2016; Collaborative Hincmar Project translations) if correctly attributed
untranslatedHighlights: Uncertain authorship; pseudo-Hincmar material likely untranslated

name: Concilia varia
modernTranslations: Collective conciliar documents; ecumenical council decrees translated in Tanner, Decrees of the Ecumenical Councils (Georgetown UP); local/provincial councils largely untranslated
untranslatedHighlights: Collection of council documents; not a single-author work

name: Aeneas Parisiensis
modernTranslations: Liber adversus Graecos (c.858-870) documented; translation status unclear but referenced in scholarship
untranslatedHighlights: Bishop of Paris; major theological work against Byzantines documented but translation coverage limited

name: Faustinus
modernTranslations: Luciferian presbyter; De trinitate and Libellus precum documented; limited English translation of his own works
untranslatedHighlights: 4th-century presbyter; works documented in Latin but comprehensive English translation lacking

name: Dungalus Reclusus
modernTranslations: Carmina (poems) and theological writings documented; no modern English translation located
untranslatedHighlights: Irish monk/recluse (fl.811-828); theological and astronomical works in Latin; English translation unclear

name: Auctor incertus (Robertus Paululus?)
modernTranslations: De officiis ecclesiasticis (12th c., PL 177:381-438), attribution uncertain; no English translation located
untranslatedHighlights: Liturgical commentary on church ceremonies/offices remains untranslated

name: Athanasius Alexandrinus
pdTranslations: NPNF2-04: Athanasius: Select Works and Letters (Newman translation, revised by Robertson)
modernTranslations: Multiple modern editions; Life of Antony widely translated; comprehensive English coverage
untranslatedHighlights: Major church father; extensive English translation availability through NPNF and modern editions

name: Pippinus Francorum
modernTranslations: No personal writings known; historical figure documented in chronicles by others (Fredegar continuator, etc.)
untranslatedHighlights: Pepin the Short; administrative figure; PL entry is likely charters/capitularies

name: Stephanus de Mureto
modernTranslations: Stephen of Muret (c.1045-1124): Maxims translated by Deborah van Doel (Cistercian Publications, 2002)
untranslatedHighlights: Grandmontine founder; Maxims translated; Liber sententiarum documented in PL

name: Conventus Parisiensis
modernTranslations: Acta of the Paris assembly (synod of 825 on images, convened by Louis the Pious); collective document, no English translation located
untranslatedHighlights: Acta on image veneration; collective/conciliar entry, not a single author
